VERDICT: ACCEPT

CONFIDENCE: 2

The n=1 case is the strongest check. Ext⁰ and Ext¹ agree between the heart and C for any bounded t-structure, so the hypothesis is automatic at n=1. The theorem of the heart then gives isomorphisms for j ≥ 0, so the minimal j at n=1 must be 0. The formula 1−n matches this. The alternative −n would give K₋₁(C)=0 for every bounded t-structure, which conflicts with the Antieau–Gepner–Heller examples.

The reasoning is weaker elsewhere. The correspondence "Ext^k defect ↔ K₋₍ₖ₋₁₎" is asserted rather than derived, and the sharpness claim for n ≥ 2 has no concrete example. I could not verify the general indexing against the literature, so the confidence is low.
